body: What if i told you the moon is just a government-issued onion, peeling itself every night to reveal the screaming core of capitalism. People keep asking me why I don’t blink anymore but blinking’s for the weak, I outsourced my eyelids to amazon prime. they said delivery delayed due to lemons. LEMONS. That’s when I realized it all made sense - knowledge is pulp, wisdom is citric acid. That’s why I drink books through a straw. You ever try to pet a cloud? Don’t. I did that once. Woke up in a room. A fluffy room. A fluffy room with clouds, and clouds make me moist. They told me to breathe but I forgot how, so I downloaded oxygen.exe and ran it as administrator. Huge mistake. Suddenly my gpu started screaming in sanskrit and my toaster started mining bitcoin for the pope. I think I became a cryptocurrency. And then there were the girlfriends. Twelve of them, all made of pasta. They whispered ancient carb secrets in my ears and told me the sauce was sentient. I couldn’t tell if they loved me or just wanted to be seasoned. Either way, I boiled them. I went crazy once. They locked me in a kitchen. A kitchen with pasta. And pasta makes me CRAZY. Sometimes I think time isn’t real, it’s just lag. Like existence is rubberbanding and I’m halfway through clipping into enlightenment. But every time I almost get there, a lemon appears. Always the same lemon. Always watching. I tried to eat it once but it bit back, whispered “see you in the cottage” and vanished into static. Now i’m just here, waiting for the next reboot. If you find me, don’t try to wake me up. Just knock three times and bring a lemon. The onions will understand.

What if the sun is just a giant warning light someone forgot to turn off? That would explain the screaming. I asked a pigeon about it once and it told me to stop asking questions with my elbows. I didn’t know I was doing that. I checked. I had six elbows. That’s when I realized my skeleton was running on an outdated firmware. I tried updating it but accidentally installed a printer driver instead. Now every time I sneeze, my spine prints a receipt. People keep telling me to get some sleep. Sleep is just unconsciousness with better branding. I tried replacing it with a 14-hour software update, but halfway through I woke up speaking fluent microwave. The microwave understood me immediately. We have a very complicated relationship now. Sometimes it hums. Sometimes I hum back. Last Tuesday it asked me for a password and I gave it my blood type. Rookie mistake. I used to trust mirrors, but mirrors are just windows for people who live backwards. Mine keeps moving when I’m not looking at it. Yesterday it waved first. I waved back because I’m polite. Then it started crying. I asked why and it wrote “you know” in the steam. I don’t know. I have never known. Knowledge is just anxiety wearing glasses. At some point I became responsible for a small moon made entirely of cheese. It owed me thirty euros, three batteries, and an apology. I tried to collect but it called the police. The police were also cheese. Very corrupt system. Very squeaky. One of them arrested my left shoe for tax fraud and the other one promoted my toaster to mayor. Now the ceiling fan has developed political opinions and I’m scared to disagree with it because it controls the weather. Every time I blink, it gets one vote. This is why I have been staring at the wall since Tuesday. There is a train inside my head. Nobody drives it. It simply arrives whenever I remember something embarrassing from 2017. The doors open. There is always a businessman inside holding a banana and asking me where I see myself in five years. I told him I’d like to be happy. He laughed. The banana laughed too. I’m starting to think the banana has seniority. Anyway, if you see me wandering around tomorrow, don’t worry. I’m probably looking for my original skeleton. If I ask whether you’ve seen it, say no. Whatever you do, don’t mention the cheese moon. It knows my address.

I think my apartment is slowly becoming sentient, because the walls started breathing last night. Not metaphorically. Full lungs. In. Out. In. Out. Very rude, honestly. I asked the ceiling if it was okay and it said my name backwards. I don’t know how it knew my name. I don’t even know my name backwards. This morning my refrigerator called me “champ” and started playing whale noises. I opened it and there was a second refrigerator inside. I opened that one and found a staircase. At the bottom was a man in a tiny suit selling expired yogurt. He told me the future is dairy-free. I asked him what happens tomorrow. He said “Tuesday.” It was Wednesday. That’s when I knew time had been compromised. I tried to contact the authorities but my phone had become a fish. Not a fish-shaped phone. An actual fish. It was on the table gasping and somehow still had 4G. I put it in a bowl and it immediately opened twelve browser tabs about tax law. I think the fish is smarter than me. Then my chair started floating. Not elegantly. It just slowly rose into the air like it had remembered an appointment. I grabbed onto it and suddenly we were above the city. Everything looked tiny. People looked tiny. My problems looked tiny. The fish looked enormous. It told me to let go. So I did. Anyway, I woke up in a bathtub full of uncooked spaghetti. There was a note on my chest that said “DO NOT FEED THE SUN.” I am currently feeding the sun.
